To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the system availability and life cycle cost of a repairable system can be optimized by adjusting the following factors: (1) the number and type of spares; (2) the number and types of technicians available to perform maintenance tasks; and (3) the repair times.
the system configuration and technician availability have the most impact on system availability.
The cost of a system is not only the initial cost, but also the cost of maintaining the system over its life.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method for the determination of optimum system availability and optimum system life cycle cost.
determining the best configuration for a given set of system constraints, and with the development of a computer model to aid the project manager in the determination of the optimum configuration.
the development of an algorithm which can be used to determine the optimum availability and life cycle cost trade-off for a given system configuration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the system life cycle costs and availability is directly related to the system configuration, equipment reliability and maintainability, and the technicians response time to failures.
a system with a high reliability and a high maintainability will be more expensive to design than one with a low reliability and low maintainability, but will have a lower life cycle cost.
the best system is the one that meets the requirements at the lowest life cycle cost.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a practical method of optimizing the life cycle costs of a system versus the availability has been developed.
the system availability is a function of equipment reliability and maintainability and system configuration and technician's response time to equipment failure.
the best way to optimize system availability is to optimize system life cycle costs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the project manager must be involved in the system design process to ensure that the system is designed to meet the life cycle cost objectives.
there are many factors that influence the availability of a system, and that the availability of a particular system can be increased by making trade-offs among the factors.
the cost of a system is a function of its availability.
